bc_centre_stage.blurb: Centre Stage is a bolted wall in the Amphitheater section of KLO Creek, in the Okanagan near Kelowna. It has five sport routes: one around the low end of 5.10 and four in the 5.12 range, so it suits strong climbers more than newcomers. This is the highest part of the Amphitheater cliff, and a cave divides it down the middle. The climbing is steep and technical, on smears and crimps. The way up starts on the switchbacks of the spur, taking the right-hand branch.

bc_upper_deck_2.blurb: Upper Deck sits on the slope above most of the other Comox Lake crags on Vancouver Island, with views over the lake and toward the Forbidden Plateau. It has five routes, four bolted and one trad, graded from 5.8 up to a single 5.11, with most of them in the 5.8 to 5.9 range. The easier lines make it a reasonable place for newer leaders. The cliff picks up sun early and late in the day and has good shade around the middle of the day. A short, low crag called Lower Deck sits on the access trail beneath it.

bc_the_prow_south.blurb: The Prow - South is a section of The Prow, one of the larger walls in Skaha Bluffs near Penticton, in the Doctors' Group. The wall holds relatively few routes, and this section has five: four trad lines and one sport route, graded between 5.10 and 5.11. Some of the lines run two pitches. It is a place for climbers who already lead at that level and carry a rack, rather than a quick bolted warm-up stop. The walk in leaves the main trail from the lower parking area near Doctors' Wall and follows a side path to the base.
